item.title: DFAT-1111: Mid-Term Review of the Climate Resilient Communities Program
item.description:
The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) is seeking a suitably qualified evaluation team to assess Climate Resilient Communities' (CRC) progress, performance, effectiveness, efficiency, governance arrangements and value for money midway through implementation.

The review will examine CRC’s contribution to climate resilience programming, climate integration across the development program, and capability strengthening within DFAT, as well as the performance of the CRC Support Unit and broader delivery arrangements.

Services sought include review planning and design, document and data analysis, stakeholder consultations, survey design and implementation, field-based data collection, preparation of an aide memoire, presentations to stakeholders, and delivery of draft and final evaluation reports containing evidence-based findings and recommendations to inform the remainder of Phase 1 implementation and potential Phase 2 activation.

Open Arms – Veterans & Families Counselling (Open Arms) is a leading provider of military-aware and trauma-informed mental health and counselling services to Australia’s military community which is administered by the Department of Veterans’ Affairs (the Department).  

The Department engages Outreach Providers through an existing panel arrangement which includes counselling and group programs for veterans and their families, and clinical supervision for Open Arms clinicians.

item.title: PROC-9177460: Australian Grains Industry Community Trust Collaboration Blueprint.
item.description:
Trust among rural and urban communities is vital to ensure Australian grain growers are able to conduct business with minimal disruption and continue to innovate and adopt new technologies. In many cases, trust is something that only becomes apparent when it is broken or tested.

 

Poor levels of trust within an industry make it more likely to be under high levels of scrutiny for practices used on farm, more likely to struggle with talent attraction for future workforce requirements (both on farm and in support and research roles) and reduce the ability for innovation, such as automation, to be adopted as commonplace on farm. There is a high risk that not addressing or maintaining current levels of trust within the grains sector will lead to future challenges impacting grain producers ability to maintain profitability and adopt new technology.

item.title: 2026-27RFQ006: Systematic Reviews to inform the updated NHMRC Statement on Electronic Cigarettes
item.description:
The Department of Health, Disability and Ageing has provided funding to NHMRC to develop an updated Statement on Electronic Cigarettes (the updated Statement) to replace the 2022 NHMRC CEO Statement on Electronic Cigarettes (the 2022 Statement). The aim of the updated NHMRC Statement is to better understand the current evidence relevant to e-cigarettes and their impacts on individual and population health.

The Electronic Cigarettes Advisory Committee (the Committee), in prioritising topic areas for review in the updated Statement, have advised that two new research questions should be answered by systematic review to inform the updated Statement. These topics are:

  1. Health and wellbeing impacts of electronic cigarettes on young people
  2. Motivators, barriers and enablers for vaping cessation

NHMRC is seeking a Supplier to undertake systematic reviews of the evidence on one or both of the topics to inform the updated Statement.

item.title: PROC-9177462: Developing acid-soil-tolerant faba bean varieties to expand faba bean adaption.
item.description: Faba bean is an important pulse crop in Australian farming systems, providing valuable rotational benefits through biological nitrogen fixation, disease breaks and improved productivity of subsequent crops. However, production and expansion of the crop are constrained by soil acidity, particularly in Western Australia, parts of South Australia and southern New South Wales, where acidic soils reduce root growth, nodulation, nitrogen fixation and grain yield. Recent advances in genetics, genomics and phenotyping technologies provide new opportunities to accelerate the development of faba bean varieties with improved adaptation to acid soils. This investment will identify novel sources of acid soil tolerance, develop molecular markers and high throughput screening methods, and deliver breeder ready germplasm for Australian breeding programs. The goal is to improve adaptation, yield stability and productivity of faba bean in acid soil environments, supporting expansion into suitable production regions and improving the profitability and resilience of Australian farming systems. Ultimately, this investment will provide the tools and germplasm required to accelerate breeding for improved acid soil tolerance in Australian faba bean.

item.title: PROC-9177463: Enhancing faba bean seed colour and seed size uniformity to increase the value of faba beans and reduce risk of classifi
item.description: Faba bean is one of Australia’s major pulse crops and an important export commodity, with premium food markets placing strong emphasis on visual grain quality. Seed coat colour stability and seed size uniformity are key determinants of grain classification, market acceptance and price, yet deterioration in seed appearance during storage and handling can increase the risk of quality downgrades and reduce grower returns. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, digital phenotyping, genomics and molecular breeding provide new opportunities to accelerate genetic improvement of these traits. This investment will develop the knowledge, genetic resources and breeding tools required to improve seed coat colour stability and seed size uniformity in Australian faba bean, including identification of valuable genetic variation, development of high throughput phenotyping and imaging technologies, molecular marker discovery and delivery of breeder ready germplasm to Australian breeding programs. Ultimately, this investment will provide the tools and germplasm required to accelerate breeding for improved visual grain quality, helping maintain access to premium markets, reduce quality downgrades and strengthen the long-term competitiveness and value of the Australian faba bean industry.
